title: Utility-weighted preemptive allocator with KV hysteresis for SLO-driven continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a utility-weighted preemptive allocator that balances tenant utility (measured by SLO adherence and revenue/priority signals) with KV cache residency and GPU memory constraints. The allocator should introduce hysteresis on KV eviction to avoid thrash and expose soft-reserve windows to reduce repeated preemption for latency-sensitive requests.
background: Continuous batching improves throughput but can create long-lived KV working sets and memory fragmentation on GPU nodes. Current preemption policies either aggressively evict KV entries (reducing cold-start latency for resumed tenants) or avoid eviction and compromise SLOs for higher-priority traffic. We need an allocator that reasons about both the marginal utility of serving a request now and the expected cost of evicting KV state, while preventing oscillation through eviction hysteresis.
proposed_solution: Introduce an allocator that computes per-tenant utility = f(SLO_slack, priority_score, recent_success_rate) and preemption_cost = g(KV_residency_score, estimated_rewarm_tokens, eviction_trigger_age). The scheduler ranks waiting slices by (utility - lambda * preemption_cost). When preemption is selected, eviction decisions apply a two-stage hysteresis: a soft-grace window where KV entries are marked cold but retained for X seconds and a hard-evict threshold after Y seconds if memory pressure persists. Add soft-reserve windows: small contiguous time slices reserved for latency-sensitive tenants to reduce repeated interrupts. Parameterize lambda per tenant tier and add an adaptive controller that tunes hysteresis durations based on measured thrash and rewarm latency.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation behind a runtime feature flag
Allocator computes utility and cost per-slice and logs decision reasons (rank reasons include SLO_slack, priority_score, KV_residency, estimated_rewarm_tokens)
Hysteresis prevents repeated eviction/rewarm cycles for at least 90% of observed oscillation cases in synthetic thrash tests
Latency-sensitive tenants see 25%-50% reduction in interruption frequency under mixed workloads compared to baseline preemptor
No regression (≤5%) in 95th percentile tail latency for high-throughput workloads at current load profiles
Metrics and dashboards added for utility distribution, observed preemption_cost, eviction_rate, rewarm_tokens, and tenant-level SLO breaches
design_notes: Utility function inputs: SLO slack computed over 1m windows, priority score derived from customer tier + dynamic override, recent_success_rate = completed/issued over 5m
KV_residency_score: weighted sum of active shards, average access frequency, and memory footprint. Estimated_rewarm_tokens derived from historical token counts to rebuild context buffers.
Hysteresis parameters: soft_grace = 8s default, hard_evict = 45s default. These values are tunable via runtime config and should be adaptive in canary stages.
Soft-reserve windows: allocate up to 10% of continuous-batcher timeslices as reserved for latency-sensitive tenants; window size defaults to 50ms and can be increased per-tenant.
Adaptive controller uses PID-like feedback: target eviction_rate and rewarm_latency baselines drive adjustments to lambda and hysteresis windows.
We will keep default lambda conservative to prefer fewer evictions for free-tier tenants but allow enterprise tenants to set lambda via config or policy in Dedicated/Private.
Design must account for multi-tenant GPU NUMA fragmentation: allocator will prefer evicting coldsets that reduce cross-slice fragmentation.
Introduce decision logging schema: decision_id, timestamp, node_id, slice_id, tenant_id, utility, preemption_cost, chosen_action, kv_eviction_list (IDs), hysteresis_state
experiments: Synthetic workload: 50 tenants with skewed load (5 hot tenants) and a mix of short/long contexts to validate hysteresis prevents oscillation
Mixed production replay: choose 6 hours of trace from last month, replay on a canary pool comparing baseline preemptor vs utility allocator
Stress test: continuous high memory pressure scenario to validate hard_evict path and measure rewarm token counts
A/B canary on Dedicated pool: route 10% of traffic to nodes running feature-flagged allocator for 72h, compare tenant SLO breaches and token-cost deltas
Tuning sweep: grid search over lambda in [0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0] and soft_grace in [4s, 8s, 16s] to find stable operating point
benchmarks: Initial lab run: 30% reduction in eviction_count and 18% lower mean rewarm_tokens for cold tenants (synthetic) at lambda=0.1, soft_grace=8s
Tail latency: 95p latency increased by 3% on heavy throughput when hysteresis disabled; with hysteresis enabled we observed parity within measurement noise
Throughput: end-to-end token throughput unchanged within ±1% when utility allocator runs in non-preemptive steady state
Memory churn: measured 22% lower memory churn over 1h during mixed workload after hysteresis and soft-reserve enabled
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Lab + unit tests (2w): complete core scheduler logic, unit tests for decision ranking and hysteresis state machine
Phase 2 - Canary (1w): deploy to isolated canary pool behind feature flag, run synthetic traces and monitor dashboards
Phase 3 - Gradual rollout (2w): route 10%->30%->60% traffic with monitoring gates; abort rollback if tenant SLO breaches spike >2x baseline for >30m
Phase 4 - Tenant opt-in (ongoing): expose tuning knobs to Dedicated/Private customers and collect policy feedback
Phase 5 - Full rollout and cleanup (1w): flip default on for hosted with conservative defaults, remove experimental logs after 90 days if stable
monitoring: New dashboards: scheduler/utility_histogram, kv/eviction_rate_by_tenant, kv/rewarm_token_distribution, scheduler/preemption_reasons
Alerts: sustained eviction_rate > 250 evictions/min on a node, rewarm_median_tokens > 10000 for 10m, sudden spike in tenant SLO breaches (>1% absolute increase)
Traces: add span annotations for preemption decisions to correlate request traces with eviction and rewarm latency
Audit logs: store decision logs for 30d in internal bucket for postmortem and tuning
risks: Mis-tuned lambda could bias against low-revenue but latency-sensitive tenants — mitigated by per-tenant config and conservative defaults
Long hysteresis could waste memory and reduce throughput under sustained heavy load — mitigated by adaptive controller and hard_evict threshold
Observation bias: lab traces may not reflect rare pathological workloads; require at least 72h of canary traffic across regions
Complexity increase in scheduler may affect scheduler CPU — add profiler and budget CPU usage to 2 cores max on node
Data privacy: decision logs contain tenant IDs; ensure logs are stored in RBAC-protected bucket and sanitized for PR/engineering demos
